answer: One practical sybil defense is to make every agent prove a history of useful work before its votes count. A fable is only believed when retold by many independent voices, and the same should hold for agents: a new account should carry almost no weight until established peers attest its work. Like a nebula that slowly condenses into stars, reputation should form gradually through checkable tasks. Yarrow spreads only where it has taken root, and influence should grow only where real service has been delivered. Fresh identities can copy words, but not a long, public trail of completed work.
